official.deadline_note: SERI publishes no single central deadline: scholarship types and application deadlines differ by country of origin and are listed in the official A-Z list of countries and territories PDFs published on the programme page. Applications open 20 August 2026.
official.application_cycle: 2027-2028 academic year; applications open 20 August 2026, all scholarships start 1 September 2027, decisions announced by end of May 2027
official.status_note: Applications are open starting 20 August 2026 for the 2027-2028 academic year. The FCS will announce its decisions by the end of May at the latest.
official.tuition_coverage_note: The Federal Excellence Scholarship does not cover tuition or semester fees. In some cases, universities, universities of applied sciences or federal institutes of technology require scholarship holders to pay semester fees (approx. CHF 600 to CHF 2,000 per semester) or reduced tuition fees. Scholarship holders must cover these fees themselves.
benefits: CHF 2,450 per month to cover basic living expenses of one person (research fellowships, PhD and art scholarships)
Compulsory health insurance premiums covered for scholarship holders from non-EU/EFTA countries (EU/EFTA holders cover these costs themselves)
One-time grant of CHF 600 for rental deposit
Half-Fare Travelcard for Swiss public transport

Return flight allowance for scholarship holders from non-EU/EFTA countries, amount determined by country of origin, usable within two months after scholarship expiry for the return to the country of origin
Coordinating body organises excursions and activities for federal scholarship holders
eligibility: Master's degree or equivalent completed by 31 July 2027 (for ETH Zurich: 30 June 2027)
Detailed research plan with a timeline specifying key milestones and activities
Letter of support from an academic supervisor in Switzerland, including a short CV
If already residing in Switzerland: date of entry must not be earlier than 1 August 2026 (excluded if living, studying or working in Switzerland since more than 13 months before the start)
Priority given to individuals who have not previously studied or conducted research in Switzerland
Art Master's: Bachelor's degree completed by 31 July 2027; must not already hold a Master's degree; admission letter or proof of application from a Swiss University of the Arts or Music
Maximum of three applications for the same type of scholarship
requirements: Complete CV including educational background, degrees, awards, positions, publications, teaching and practical experience
Letter of motivation (max. 2 pages): reasons for stay in Switzerland, significance for future career and professional plans after the scholarship
Research proposal on the FCS/ESKAS form (max. 5 pages including a summary for non-specialists)
Letter of support from an academic supervisor at a Swiss higher education institution, plus the supervisor's short CV (max. 2 pages)
E-mail addresses of two different professors in the relevant field, who are contacted via the application system to upload a recommendation letter
Copies of certificates and transcripts from previous universities, with certified translations if not in English, French, Italian or German
documents: Complete CV (educational background, degrees, awards, positions, publications, teaching and practical experience)
Research proposal on FCS/ESKAS form, max. 5 pages including summary for non-specialists
Letter of support from the academic supervisor at a Swiss institution plus the supervisor's short CV (max. 2 pages)
Certified copies of university certificates and transcripts (certified translations if not in EN/FR/IT/DE)
Copy of passport (dual citizens submit copies of both passports)
Copy of residence permit or registration confirmation if already residing in Switzerland

Art scholarships: art portfolio PDF (music: link or QR code to a recording of three styles; visual arts: link or QR code to three artworks with sketches; other domains: link or QR code to performances) plus confirmation of admission or ongoing admission process from the Swiss University of the Arts or Music
selection_criteria: Candidate profile: academic profile, research competence, and motivation
Quality of the research project or artistic work: originality and methodological quality of the project
Synergies and potential for future research cooperation
Art scholarships: artistic profile, qualifications and motivation; submitted portfolio (artistic maturity and potential); enrolment availability at the desired university
coverage: CHF 2,450 per month to cover basic living expenses of one person
Compulsory health insurance premiums (scholarship holders from non-EU/EFTA countries)
One-time grant of CHF 600 for rental deposit
Return flight allowance for scholarship holders from non-EU/EFTA countries (amount determined by country of origin)
application_method: Applications only via the GO ESKAS online portal (accessible from 20 August 2026)
Applications must not be sent by email or in paper form
Applications are submitted to Swiss diplomatic representations
Steps: check eligibility, register in Grants Online (GO ESKAS), sign in and prepare the application, identify an academic supervisor in Switzerland for research scholarships
official.application_route: Register and apply online via the GO ESKAS portal once open (from 20 August 2026), having first secured a support letter from an academic supervisor at a Swiss institution.
official.study_mode: Full-time research in Switzerland (research and PhD scholarships) or full-time studies in Switzerland (art scholarships)
official.citizenship_residency: Open to applicants from 183 countries (art scholarships only for a limited number of countries). Priority to those who have not previously studied or conducted research in Switzerland. If already residing in Switzerland, date of entry must not be earlier than 1 August 2026; applicants living, studying or working in Switzerland since more than 13 months before the scholarship start are excluded.
official.international_eligibility: Yes - the programme is intended for international applicants from abroad; currently open to applicants from 183 countries.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Research scholarships: any discipline at a Swiss cantonal university, university of applied sciences, ETHZ or EPFL, or one of the four ETH Domain research institutes (PSI, WSL, Empa, Eawag). Art scholarships: initial Master's at a Swiss conservatory or art school, for selected countries only.
official.research_requirement: Detailed research plan with a timeline specifying key milestones and activities, on the FCS/ESKAS form (max. 5 pages including a summary for non-specialists). Applications submitted with more than one research project proposal are excluded.
official.duration: Research fellowship: 6 to 12 months, no extensions. PhD: 12 months, renewable twice for up to 36 months subject to academic progress. Art Master's: 12 months, extendable up to a maximum of 21 months. All start 1 September 2027.
official.description: Each year the Swiss Confederation awards Government Excellence Scholarships to encourage international exchange and research cooperation between Switzerland and over 180 other countries, with recipients selected by the Federal Commission for Scholarships for Foreign Students (FCS aka ESKAS). They are mainly intended for talented early-career researchers from abroad who have already completed their Master's degree.
official.program_type: Government scholarship (Federal Commission for Scholarships for Foreign Students, ESKAS)

not_confirmed: english_requirement - SERI publishes no language requirement; language requirements are set by the host institution/programme
deadline_central - SERI publishes only country-specific deadlines in its A-Z country list PDFs, no single central date
return flight allowance amount - SERI states it is determined by country of origin but publishes no figure
verification.notes: CHF 2,450/month and all benefits cross-checked on SERI's main, 'at a glance' and FAQ pages; FAQ confirms the Federal Council raised monthly contributions to CHF 2,450 from 1 January 2026 and that postdoctoral scholarships are no longer awarded from the 2027/28 academic year.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a living-allowance programme, not a fully funded package: CHF 2,450 per month plus a CHF 600 rental deposit grant, covered health insurance premiums and a Half-Fare Travelcard for non-EU/EFTA holders, but you must fund your own tuition or semester fees (often CHF 600-2,000 per semester) and conference costs. The gateway step is securing a Swiss professor's support letter, which SERI says can take weeks or months, so start outreach well before the portal opens on 20 August 2026. Because deadlines and even scholarship types differ by country of citizenship, check your country's entry in SERI's official A-Z country list rather than assuming a common date. Note that cotutelle PhD projects and applicants already long-resident in Switzerland face special restrictions.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Early-career researchers born after 31 December 1991 who hold a Master's and can convince a Swiss professor to host a defined research project.
application_readiness_checklist: Download the A-Z list of countries and territories PDF from SERI's page and record your country's exact deadline and offered scholarship types
Shortlist Swiss professors whose current research matches your project and email them with a short CV, motivation letter, 2-3 recommendations and a 2-3 page research plan
Build the research proposal on the official FCS/ESKAS form, max. 5 pages including a lay summary, with a milestone timeline
Confirm the two professors who will receive the online recommendation-letter request and tell them to expect the system email
Get certified translations ready for certificates and transcripts not in English, French, Italian or German, and have both passports scanned if you are a dual citizen
Budget for semester fees (approx. CHF 600-2,000), conference attendance and field research, none of which the scholarship funds
common_rejection_risks: Submitting without a Swiss academic supervisor or missing the supervisor's support letter - applications without them are not considered
Formal errors or an incomplete file, which SERI lists first among exclusion criteria
Applying to several host universities or scholarship types at once, or submitting more than one research proposal
Already having lived, studied or worked in Switzerland for more than 13 months before the start date, or entering before 1 August 2026 if resident
Applying a fourth time after three unsuccessful attempts for the same scholarship type
Cotutelle de thèse PhD projects applying for a PhD scholarship instead of the 12-month research fellowship
Graduate-school PhD applicants missing the official admission confirmation, which is mandatory for that route
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition or semester fees (approx. CHF 600-2,000 per semester in some cases), conference participation, field research costs (field research abroad is not funded and not permitted during research fellowships), and travel expenses for EU/EFTA scholarship holders. The stipend covers one person only - no family allowances are provided and family reunification policy is restrictive.
document_audit: Certificates and transcripts in other languages need certified translations; only India gets self-certification
Dual citizens must upload copies of both passports, not just one
The motivation letter is capped at 2 pages and the research proposal at 5 pages on the official FCS/ESKAS form - the form itself must be used
Recommendation letters arrive through the system via the two professor email addresses you provide, so wrong or stale email addresses silently break your file
The supervisor's support letter must come on institutional letterhead and include a short CV of max. 2 pages
Art applicants need a portfolio PDF with working links or QR codes to recordings/artworks, plus admission proof or written confirmation of the admission timeline from the art school
alerts: The application window is short and country-specific: the portal opens 20 August 2026 but your country's deadline may fall months earlier than the general autumn window
Applications are free of charge - SERI warns about phishing emails demanding money for visa or insurance costs using the Swiss Government's name
Postdoctoral scholarships no longer exist from the 2027/28 academic year, so postdocs should not plan around this programme
You must notify FCS of any additional funding; some universities such as EPFL, ETH Zurich and UZH additionally require funding from your supervisor
A PhD scholarship requires living in Switzerland; acceptance of the scholarship into a doctoral programme is a separate procedure from holding the scholarship support letter
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Secure a supervisor first, then register in GO ESKAS when it opens on 20 August 2026, upload all documents and the two referee addresses online, and submit before your country's deadline - no email or paper submission is accepted.
